ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is marked with the 50°E and 55°E meridians and the 25°N parallel. Oil fields and gas fields are mainly distributed in the gulf coastal area around about 50°E—55°E and near 25°N. The legend text shows “oil field” and “gas field.” This location and resource distribution characteristics correspond to the petroleum and natural gas production area of the Persian Gulf in West Asia. Reasoning: When the largest oil-producing country in the area shown supplies petroleum to our country, the starting point is on the coast of the Persian Gulf, and shipping to China needs first to leave the Persian Gulf and enter the Indian Ocean; the question asks “when reaching our country, which strait does it still need to pass through,” that is, besides the relevant strait at the outlet of the Persian Gulf, to continue eastward into the South China Sea and China’s coastal waters, it usually needs to pass through the Strait of Malacca in Southeast Asia. Therefore the answer is the Strait of Malacca.
